name: When should I consider replacing my deck boards instead of just repairing them?

mainEntity.name: When should I consider replacing my deck boards instead of just repairing them?

acceptedAnswer.text: You should consider replacing deck boards when there is widespread damage such as extensive rot, deep cracks, splintering, or significant warping that compromises the deck's structural integrity or safety. Minor issues like a few loose boards or small areas of surface wear can often be repaired. Replacing boards is often more cost-effective and safer in the long run if the damage affects a large portion of the deck or if the boards are nearing the end of their lifespan. When evaluating, consider the overall condition of the deck substructure as well; if the joists and beams are sound, board replacement is a viable option.
acceptedAnswer.description: Replace deck boards for widespread damage like extensive rot, deep cracks, or significant warping that affects safety or structure, rather than just minor repairs.
